correctness.rationale: For closed-range K, K* is bounded below on R(K), so any surviving K-frame subfamily projects to a frame in R(K), establishing E_K≤E(P_RΦ). If all atoms lie in R(K), the reverse implication follows from ‖K*f‖≤‖K‖‖P_Rf‖. For near K-Riesz families, projecting the deletable K-Riesz basis is an ordinary Riesz basis. For each N≥2 an orthonormal basis of R^N with all first coordinates 1/sqrt(N), and K the rank-one e1 projection, loses K-frame property after deleting ANY atom while its N identical projected nonzero atoms allow N−1 deletions. This is a uniform symbolic construction, not extrapolation from the N=2 example.
